questions.stemHtml: Which body is the statutory regulator of the securities (stock) market in India?

options.textHtml: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)

questions.solutionHtml:
C is correct. SEBI, given statutory powers under the SEBI Act, 1992, regulates the securities market, protects investors and supervises intermediaries such as stock exchanges and brokers.

A RBI is the central bank and regulates banks and monetary policy. B NITI Aayog is a policy think tank with no regulatory role. D IRDAI regulates insurance.

questions.stemHtml: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India established?
questions.solutionHtml:
A is correct. The RBI was set up under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and began operations on 1 April 1935.

C 1949 is the year the RBI was nationalised. D 1969 is the year of the nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks. B 1947 is the year of Independence, not the RBI's founding.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Reserve Bank of India?

options.textHtml: Acting as banker to the Government
Acting as lender of last resort to banks

questions.solutionHtml:
D is correct. Income tax is administered by the Income Tax Department under the Central Board of Direct Taxes (Ministry of Finance), not by the RBI.

A, B and C are classic central-bank functions of the RBI: it manages the Government's banking transactions, provides emergency liquidity to banks as lender of last resort, and has the sole right to issue currency notes (other than the one-rupee note, which is issued by the Government).

questions.stemHtml: NITI Aayog was constituted in 2015 to replace which body?

options.textHtml: Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Department

questions.solutionHtml:
B is correct. NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was set up on 1 January 2015 in place of the Planning Commission. It functions as the Government's policy think tank and promotes cooperative federalism; unlike the Planning Commission, it does not allocate funds to states.

A The Finance Commission is a constitutional body (Article 280) and continues to exist. C and D were not replaced by NITI Aayog.

questions.stemHtml: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) introduced in India is best described as a

options.textHtml: direct tax levied on the income of manufacturers
destination-based tax on the consumption of goods and services
tax on the wealth held by individuals
origin-based tax collected only by the state where goods are produced

questions.solutionHtml:
B is correct. GST is an indirect tax on the supply of goods and services. It is destination-based: the tax revenue accrues to the state where the goods or services are consumed, not where they are produced. Input tax credit at each stage means only the value added is effectively taxed.

A and C describe direct taxes (on income or wealth), whereas GST is indirect. D reverses the principle — GST is destination-based, not origin-based.

questions.stemHtml: In Indian monetary policy, the repo rate is the rate at which

options.textHtml: commercial banks lend to their most creditworthy customers
the Government borrows from the public through bonds
commercial banks park their surplus funds with the RBI
the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities

questions.solutionHtml:
D is correct. 'Repo' stands for repurchase agreement: banks sell government securities to the RBI with an agreement to buy them back, which is effectively a short-term loan from the RBI at the repo rate.

C describes the reverse repo (banks lending surplus funds to the RBI). A describes a bank's lending rate to customers. B refers to government borrowing, not the repo rate.

questions.stemHtml: The Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Constitution of India?
questions.solutionHtml:
A is correct. Part III (Articles 12–35) lists the Fundamental Rights.

B Part IV contains the Directive Principles of State Policy. C Part IVA contains the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A). D Part V deals with the Union (executive, Parliament, etc.).

questions.stemHtml: The Constitution of India came into force on
questions.solutionHtml:
C is correct. The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

B 26 November 1949 is the date the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution (observed as Constitution Day); a few provisions came into force then, but the Constitution as a whole commenced on 26 January 1950. A is Independence Day. D has no constitutional significance.

questions.stemHtml: Who presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament in India?

options.textHtml: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.solutionHtml:
D is correct. A joint sitting is summoned by the President under Article 108 to resolve a deadlock over a bill, but it is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (in the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker, and then the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha).

A The President summons but does not preside. B The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha but does not preside over joint sittings. C The Prime Minister has no presiding role.

options.textHtml: protection of life and personal liberty

questions.solutionHtml:

B is Article 17, C is Article 14 and D is Article 32.

questions.solutionHtml:

questions.solutionHtml:

questions.stemHtml: The World Trade Organization (WTO), which came into being on 1 January 1995, succeeded which arrangement?

options.textHtml: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)
The United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)

questions.solutionHtml:
C is correct. The WTO was established by the Marrakesh Agreement following the Uruguay Round and replaced GATT (in force since 1948) as the institutional framework for multilateral trade rules. GATT's text survives as part of WTO law.

A created the IMF and World Bank. B is a European regional body. D UNCTAD still exists as a UN body.

A volt measures potential difference, B ohm measures resistance and C watt measures power.

questions.stemHtml: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.solutionHtml:
B is correct. Ultraviolet-B radiation in sunlight converts a cholesterol derivative in the skin into vitamin D, which helps the body absorb calcium.

A and C come mainly from diet. D Vitamin K is obtained from food and produced by gut bacteria, not by sunlight on the skin.

questions.stemHtml: The fiscal deficit of a government is defined as

options.textHtml: total expenditure minus revenue receipts only
total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings and other liabilities

questions.solutionHtml:
C is correct. Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts), i.e. total receipts excluding borrowings. It shows how much the government must borrow in the year.

B is the revenue deficit. D is the primary deficit. A ignores non-debt capital receipts (such as recovery of loans and disinvestment proceeds), so it is not the standard definition.
